newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs end strong on telecoms, power sectors.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs end strong on telecoms, power sectors.

text.p: Brazilian shares ended strong in heavy trade for a second day in a row, powered by the telecommunications and power sectors, brokers said.
The Bovespa index of the 48 most active shares closed up 1.5 percent at 11301 points, with Telebras and Eletrobras spearheading the rise.
Market volume was higher than usual at 835.9 million reais ($788.5 million), mostly due to increased foreign and particularly local buys orders.
"Local equity funds have been increasing their participation in the bolsa," said a senior trader.

Telebras stock, which accounted for over 60 percent of today's trade, has been rising ahead of the June 4 announcement of prequalified bidders for the much-awaited Band B cellular sale. Rumors that the bids presented by several consortia will be exceptionally high have been pushing telecoms shares ahead, traders said.
Telebras preferred rose 1.72 percent to 147.50 reais, while its common stock gained 1.53 percent to 139 reais.
Among other blue-chips, federal power firm Eletrobras posted the highest gains, jumping 3.12 percent to 529 reais.

Private mining giant CVRD fell 1.22 percent to 24.20 reais. Traders noted the stock is still suffering from uncertainties over the company's new management after a group led by steelmaker CSN bought control of the miner.

Cemig stocks lost ground following today's sale of a 32.9 percent voting stake in the firm to a U.S.-led group. Traders said the stock's poor performance reflected market disappointment with the outcome of the closely watched auction, which attracted only one bidder.
Brokers expect the market to continue rising, but it will probably lose some strength Friday when the local bolsas resume trade after Thursday's Corpus Christi holiday.
